occupation-list: What do the positions in this list label before any numbers are written into them?
How would you count the total when both entries in the list contain particles?
fermion-occupation: A complete electron state includes more than its spatial pattern. Which remaining label can differ?
List all the labels of both electrons before deciding whether their complete states coincide.
boson-creation: Check whether multiplying a ket by a factor leaves it normalized. Can a probability exceed one?
Distinguish the coefficient written outside the ket from the occupation number written inside it.
pair-interaction: List the pairs AB and BA. Did you find two distinct pairs or count the same pair twice?
Would counting pairs of marbles use any information about their electric charges?
boson-removal: Compare the length of the normalized vacuum with the result of trying to remove a particle from an empty mode.
Is it the energy label or the occupation count that controls the removal rule?
number-operator: Imagine counting the particles in several snapshots. Would averaging your counts require breaking up a particle in any one snapshot?
Try averaging two different whole-number readings. What numbers can an average take?
boson-commutator: Try adding and then removing a particle in an initially empty mode. Now try the opposite order.
The correction in the commutator is fixed. Does a larger occupation make a fixed correction exactly zero?
fermion-sign: Find the squared size of an amplitude before and after multiplying the entire state by −1.
Does the distinction between a shared sign and a relative sign depend on the particle species?
boson-hopping: What does the hopping operator produce before a state is normalized or a transition probability is computed?
Check the units and normalization of the whole calculation before treating one factor as a probability.
bose-hubbard: Compare the average of a hopping operator with the result of actually applying it to the starting state.
Does choosing a real coefficient forbid an amplitude for a different occupation pattern?
fermion-hubbard: List the full pair of labels for each electron, including spin.
The interaction energy changes a cost. Which part of Pauli’s rule depends on that cost?
ising-bond: Insert +1 or −1 for the two spins. Can their product vanish?
Include the minus sign in the bond energy before comparing the two spin products.
mean-field-decoupling: Expand the product with both deviations included. Under what condition would the term you omit vanish?
Averaging a product and multiplying two averages are different operations. Check the discarded correlation.
neighbor-average-field: Check the units of h in the energy rule before substituting a magnetic-field reading.
Can changing a coupling’s sign convert tesla to units of energy?
mean-field-consistency: Could a zero solution sit at a maximum or minimum? Inspect what happens just to either side.
Finding a self-consistent value is one test. What happens after a tiny perturbation?
mean-field-transition: Which neighbor-to-neighbor fluctuations did the approximation leave out of a one-dimensional chain?
Would adding more sites restore neglected local correlations automatically?
occupation-variance: Compare a preparation always giving the mean with one giving values on both sides of it.
Can a distribution still be broad around a whole-number average?
spin-variance: Could opposite spin readings cancel in the mean at some other temperature too?
Try equally common +1 and −1 readings and inspect the individual results before averaging.
collective-variance: Write out the variance of a sum. Which extra term compares how the two quantities vary together?
The spread of one quantity and the correlation between two quantities are different terms. Which of them can have a sign?
average-fluctuations: Imagine many sensors all picking up the very same fluctuation. Do they give independent readings?
A small or large mean describes the centre. What evidence would establish independent deviations?
connected-correlation: Can two ordinary, classically linked random outcomes each have zero mean?
Consider two copies of the same random bit. Could their readings be linked without any quantum state?
correlation-length: Would a distribution with several length scales naturally fit one decay length?
Units tell you how to compare separation with a length scale. Do they choose the shape of the curve?
static-structure-factor: A snapshot records spatial information. Which variable would be needed to distinguish two motions with the same snapshot?
Zero wave number selects a spatial pattern. Does it supply a time record?
fluctuation-response: Do operators in different orders give the same result just because the state is pure?
What assumptions connected an equilibrium variance to a response in the derivation?
linear-response: Draw a time axis and put the disturbance after the reading. Which direction is allowed for cause and effect?
A weak disturbance changes the size of the response. Does its size alter the order of events?
